findings.failing_input: Operator clicks 'Sync now' at 23:55 IL on May 23, 2026. The /api/operator/sync-now route fires the event. The Inngest dispatch + worker pickup typically adds a few seconds of latency — so the handler might execute at 23:55:08 IL OR (if the worker is slow / queued) at 00:00:15 IL on May 24. The `todayJerusalem()` call at line 112 evaluates at WORKER EXECUTION TIME (per the file comment at line 65-68 'resolves at function-execution time, not send time'), so a near-midnight click could resolve to either May 23 OR May 24 depending on the dispatch latency.
findings.expected: This is documented intent (file comment line 65-68 explicitly says 'so the value reflects the moment the worker picks up the event'). The operator's mental model 'refresh today's numbers right now' is consistent — if they're clicking at 00:00:15, they probably mean May 24 (the calendar date they're now in).
findings.actual: Behavior is correct per intent. Not a bug.
findings.regression_test_idea: n/a — accepted behavior, but worth documenting in a comment near the operator console call site so future operators understand the date-resolution semantics.

findings.failing_input:
/api/operator/sync-now POST body contains `{storeId: 'usmile360_typo'}`. The route dispatches `inngest.send('event/sync-now', {data: {storeId: 'usmile360_typo'}})`. The handler at line 111 destructures `storeId` from event.data — TypeScript's StoreId discriminated union is a COMPILE-time check only. At runtime, the typed cast at line 112 (`event.data as SyncNowPayload`) is a no-op. The handler invokes `runDailyForStore('usmile360_typo', ...)`.

runDailyForStore in cronDaily.ts uses storeId as: (1) a label in step.run IDs (e.g. 'fetch-shopify' — same for all stores, no IDs here), (2) the first arg to fetchShopifyDayRows / fetchMetaSpendForDay / etc. Each of those fetchers reads per-store credentials via process.env['SHOPIFY_TOKEN_USMILE360_TYPO'] (or similar). The missing env var → fetcher throws 'Missing credentials' → step.run propagates → runDailyForStore throws → Inngest retries 4× → deadletter.

Production shape: operator typo in a curl call or a future operator-console bug that doesn't validate storeIds before dispatch would burn 4 retries × 6 step.runs = ~24 wasted execs per typo. The 5xx in Inngest dashboard is the only signal.
findings.expected: Validate storeId against the canonical STORES const before invoking runDailyForStore. Throw a clear 'Invalid storeId: X' error so Inngest doesn't retry an unrecoverable input error.
findings.actual: The file comment at line 21-26 explicitly delegates runtime payload validation to 'the API route's job (plan 14) — event/sync-now itself trusts the payload it receives'. So the design intent is to NOT validate. But the trust assumption is wrong if the API route's validation has a bug or is bypassed (e.g. via direct inngest.send from a future debug tool).
findings.fix_sketch: Add `if (!STORE_IDS.has(storeId)) throw new Error(`event/sync-now: invalid storeId ${storeId}`)` before line 119. The check costs nothing at runtime and protects against caller-side bugs. Mirror the validation pattern in eventBackfill.ts:187-200.
findings.regression_test_idea: Add Test: handler({event: {data: {storeId: 'usmile360_typo'}}, step}) should reject WITHOUT calling runDailyForStore. Currently it would call runDailyForStore and the call would fail downstream (potentially with a less clear error message).

uncertainty_notes: Module is intentionally minimal (single-store sync-now wrapper around runDailyForStore). The file comment is explicit about the design decisions (trust the route, default to today, use the same step.run subset as cronDaily). INN-18 is a defense-in-depth concern: the upstream route DOES validate (per the comment at line 21-26) but layered validation is cheap and the cost-of-failure (wasted retry budget + unclear error) is real. INN-17 is documented intent. No correctness bugs in the date/dispatch/payload paths.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for invalid storeId (INN-18). Test 2 + Test 3 only exercise valid storeIds ('uzoshop'). A typo or undefined storeId would propagate to runDailyForStore unchecked.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Defense-in-depth — the API route is supposed to validate but a single typo in a future refactor that bypasses the route would silently waste retry budget.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: handler({event: {data: {storeId: 'invalid'}}, step}) should reject; runDailyForStoreMock should not be called.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for missing storeId (event.data omitted entirely or event.data.storeId === undefined). The current code destructures `{ storeId, date = todayJerusalem() }` — if storeId is undefined, runDailyForStore receives undefined.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: handler({event: {data: {}}, step}) should reject with a clear 'storeId required' error.

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test for date format validation. The `date?` field is optional but if provided is taken as-is. A malformed date like '2026-13-99' or '15/05/2026' would be passed unchanged to runDailyForStore → which would pass to Shopify / Supabase → eventual error in a downstream layer.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Same defense-in-depth pattern. Clear early-error vs unclear late-error.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: handler with date='2026-13-99' should reject with 'Invalid date format' (YYYY-MM-DD regex match).

test_coverage_gaps.description: No test asserting the date default actually evaluates at handler-execution time (vs at module-load time). The current code calls todayJerusalem() inside the destructure default — which DOES evaluate at handler call time. A regression that hoisted the call to module scope would silently freeze the default date at deployment time.
test_coverage_gaps.why_it_matters: Would cause 'Sync now' to always use the deployment-date instead of today.
test_coverage_gaps.suggested_fixture: Use vi.useFakeTimers + setSystemTime to advance time between two handler invocations; assert each call passed a different default date.
